tagline: Gravel along the ridgetops, over glades where roadrunners live.
intro: From Ava the way runs south on Highway 5 and west on Highway A to Smallett Junction, then turns south, and from there Glade Top Trail keeps to narrow ridgetops some 500 feet above a broken, rolling countryside for 23 miles. It is two lanes of all-weather gravel with quarried stone culverts and retaining walls, little changed since the Civilian Conservation Corps worked on it in the late 1930s.

The glades it is named for are sunny openings of grass and wildflowers on dolomite, with soil so shallow and shade so scarce that the Forest Service likens them to desert. Roadrunners, collared lizards, tarantulas and scorpions live in them.

moments.title: Arkansas View
moments.text: A picnic table and a horse hitch stand at the pull-out named for the next state south, and the byway's views reach forty miles that way to the Boston Mountains.

moments.title: Caney Day Use Area
moments.text: The Forest Service names this picnic ground on a glade as the view not to miss, beside Caney's old fire lookout tower, where turkey vultures sometimes sit preening.

practical: The road is gravel all the way, none of the stops has drinking water, and riding ATVs or UTVs on the byway takes a county permit.

sources.label: USDA Forest Service, Glade Top National Forest Scenic Byway
